title: Marangu Route · 5 days
content:
This package offers an exhilarating adventure for those eager to conquer Africa’s tallest peak, Mount Kilimanjaro. Your journey begins upon arrival at Kilimanjaro International Airport, where a warm welcome from our driver sets the tone for your experience. You will be transferred to your Hotel, where a delicious meal awaits, along with a pre-trekking briefing from our experienced coordinators to prepare you for the adventure ahead.

The trek commences from Moshi, taking you through the breathtaking landscapes of Kilimanjaro. You’ll start in the lush rainforest and gradually ascend to higher altitudes, allowing for acclimatization at various camps along the way. The pinnacle of this journey is the ascent to Uhuru Peak, the highest point in Africa.

Following this incredible achievement, the descent offers one last chance to appreciate the diverse scenery. After completing the trek, you will return to Sal salinero Hotel for a well-deserved rest. For those looking to extend their adventure, we offer options for safaris or relaxing beach stays in Zanzibar, creating a comprehensive Tanzanian experience.

If you want more information about the trek or any extension options, feel free to check out our detailed packages on our website.

faqs.title: How long does it take to climb Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: The duration of a Kilimanjaro climb typically ranges from 5 to 10 days, depending on the chosen route and your acclimatization needs. Longer treks allow for better acclimatization and increase the chances of reaching the summit.

faqs.title: What is the best time to climb Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: The best times to climb are during the dry seasons, which run from late June to October and from mid-January to March. These months generally offer clearer skies and better weather conditions.

faqs.title: Do I need to be an experienced climber to summit Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: No previous climbing experience is necessary to summit Kilimanjaro. However, a good level of physical fitness, preparation, and understanding of altitude sickness are important for a successful climb.

faqs.title: What are the different routes to climb Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: There are several routes to summit Kilimanjaro, including the Marangu, Machame, Lemosho, and Rongai routes. Each varies in difficulty, scenery, and duration, so choose one that aligns with your preferences and fitness level.

faqs.title: What should I pack for climbing Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: Essential gear includes layered clothing, a waterproof jacket, sturdy hiking boots, a sleeping bag rated for cold temperatures, trekking poles, a headlamp, and personal items like sunscreen, a hat, and a water bottle. Consult your tour operator for a comprehensive packing list.

faqs.title: How high is Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: Mount Kilimanjaro stands at approximately 5,895 meters (19,341 feet) above sea level, making it the highest peak in Africa.

faqs.title: What is altitude sickness, and how can I prevent it?
faqs.content: Altitude sickness occurs when your body struggles to acclimatize to high elevations, leading to symptoms like headache, nausea, and fatigue. To minimize the risk, ascend slowly, stay hydrated, and consider taking a medication like Diamox. Listen to your body and communicate with your guides.

faqs.title: Are there age restrictions for climbing Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: Yes, climbers must be at least 10 years old to trek Kilimanjaro, and those under 18 should be accompanied by an adult. Some operators have specific age limits, so check with your chosen tour company.

faqs.title: Will I need a guide to climb Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: Yes, all climbers are required to go with a licensed guide and a support team. This is essential for safety, navigation, and to comply with Tanzanian regulations.

faqs.title: What is the success rate for reaching the summit?
faqs.content: Success rates vary by route, but generally hover around 50-65% for shorter treks. Longer routes that allow for better acclimatization tend to have higher success rates, often exceeding 80%.

faqs.title: Is there a chance of communication during the climb?
faqs.content: You may have limited cell phone coverage on certain routes, but it’s advisable to expect minimal connectivity. Most trekkers focus on enjoying the experience and the beautiful surroundings rather than staying connected.

itinerary.title: Day 1
itinerary.content:
Upon your arrival at Kilimanjaro International Airport, you will be greeted by our dedicated driver, who will be holding a sign with your name, ready to offer a warm welcome. You will then enjoy a comfortable transfer to your Hotel, where you can unwind and indulge in a delicious meal. After settling in, our experienced mountain coordinators and your guide will conduct a pre-trekking briefing, giving you the chance to learn about the exciting expedition that lies ahead.

At your Hotel, you can relax in a serene environment featuring a swimming pool, a beautiful garden, and an inviting bar and restaurant. This tranquil setting is the perfect place to prepare for your adventure, ensuring you are well-rested and ready for the journey to conquer Mount Kilimanjaro.

Overnight: Sal salinero hotel or similar

itinerary.title: Day 2
itinerary.desc: Moshi to Marangu Gate | Mandara Hut
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 1,830 meters (6,004 feet) – 2,700 meters (8,858 feet)
  • Hiking distance: 8 km
  • Hiking time: 4 to 5 hours

After enjoying a hearty breakfast, you will embark on your adventure with a one-hour drive from Moshi to the Marangu Gate. At the gate, you’ll complete the necessary registration formalities before beginning your trek through the lush rainforest. The path to Mandara Hut, your first campsite, features a steady uphill hike, where you may have the chance to spot monkeys and other wildlife.

Upon your arrival at Mandara, a warm meal will await you, and you will be accommodated in comfortable A-frame huts. In the evening, you have the option to take a short acclimatization hike to Maundi Crater, which provides stunning panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. This initial trek sets the tone for your Kilimanjaro adventure, blending beautiful scenery with opportunities to adjust to the altitude.

itinerary.title: Day 3
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 2,700 meters (8,858 feet) – 3,720 meters (12,205 feet)
  • Hiking distance: 12 km
  • Hiking time: 5 to 6 hours

Begin your day with a hearty breakfast at Mandara Hut before continuing your trek through the lush rainforest, transitioning into the moorland zone. As you ascend, you’ll notice a gradual change in the vegetation, giving way to a more rugged and open landscape. The 6-hour trek to Horombo Hut promises stunning views of the Kibo and Mawenzi peaks along the way.

Upon your arrival at Horombo, a warm meal will greet you, providing the perfect opportunity to relax and acclimate to the higher altitude. In the evening, your guide will conduct a briefing for the next day’s trek, ensuring you are well-prepared for the challenges that lie ahead. This structure not only aids acclimatization but also fosters a sense of camaraderie and readiness among the group, enhancing your overall experience on this magnificent journey.

itinerary.title: Day 4
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 3,720 meters (12,205 feet) – 4,700 meters (15,419 feet)
  • Hiking distance: 10 km
  • Hiking time: 5 to 6 hours

Today’s trek takes you across the expansive lunar desert known as the “Saddle,” a stark and rugged landscape nestled between the Kibo and Mawenzi peaks. Although the terrain is desolate, the awe-inspiring views of the towering peaks on either side create a breathtaking backdrop for your hike. Expect to spend about 6 hours on this section of the journey, which allows ample time to appreciate the vastness of the landscape and the unique beauty of the surroundings.

Upon your arrival at Kibo Hut, you’ll settle in for an early dinner to help conserve your energy for the upcoming summit attempt. In the evening, your guide will provide a detailed briefing to prepare you for the final ascent, scheduled to begin just before midnight. This preparation is crucial as it sets the stage for a successful summit experience, ensuring that you’re well-informed and mentally ready for the challenges that lie ahead.

itinerary.title: Day 5
itinerary.desc: Kibo Hut | Summit Attempt | Horombo Hut
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 4,700 meters (15,419 feet) – 5,895 meters (19,341 feet) – 3,720
  • Hiking distance: 22 km
  • Hiking & descending time: 12 to 15 hours

Around midnight, you’ll awaken to begin the final ascent toward Uhuru Peak. This segment of the climb, leading to Gillman’s Point at 5,685 meters, is steep and demanding, typically taking about six hours of steady climbing. This challenging section will truly test your endurance, but your guide will be there to offer support and encouragement throughout the journey.

Upon reaching Gillman’s Point, you’ll have the opportunity to traverse the crater rim towards Uhuru Peak, the highest point in Africa. If conditions allow, you’ll be treated to a breathtaking sunrise over the continent, making this moment even more memorable. After celebrating your incredible achievement at the summit, you’ll begin your descent to Kibo Hut for a brief rest before continuing onward to Horombo Hut for the night. This part of the trek offers a chance to reflect on your journey and the stunning landscapes you’ve experienced.

itinerary.title: Day 6
itinerary.desc: Horombo Hut to Marangu Gate | Return to Moshi
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 3,720 meters (12,205 feet) – 1,830 meters (6,004 feet)
  • Hiking distance: 20 km
  • Descending time: 6 to 7 hours

After breakfast, you’ll begin your descent through the diverse moorland and lush rainforest zones, making your way back to Marangu Gate. As you trek downward, take a moment to enjoy the final views of the stunning landscapes and reflect on your remarkable achievement. Upon reaching the gate, you’ll receive your well-earned summit certificate, a testament to your hard work and determination.

Following this memorable moment, you’ll be driven back to the Hotel in Moshi, where a hot meal, refreshing shower, and comfortable bed await you. If you’re interested in extending your adventure, our safari coordinator will be available to discuss options such as an exhilarating wildlife safari or a relaxing trip to the breathtaking beaches of Zanzibar. This is the perfect opportunity to further explore the beauty and culture of Tanzania.

Overnight: Sal salinero hotel or similar

itinerary.title: Day 7
itinerary.content:
After breakfast, you’ll be transferred back to Kilimanjaro International Airport for your departure. If you wish to extend your adventure, you can add a day trip to your itinerary to explore nearby attractions or immerse yourself in local culture. For more details, we invite you to visit our Day Trip page.

Alternatively, you may choose to continue your journey with a visit to the stunning island of Zanzibar. Whether you’re seeking relaxation on pristine beaches or exploring the island’s rich culture, Zanzibar has something for everyone. Check out our Zanzibar page to discover the perfect package for your next excursion. If you’re interested in adding a safari experience, please visit our Safari page for more information on our exciting safari options.
